description: Below 1280px, a user can write, check and save a cover letter, and read it, with one task on screen at a time: - an Édition / Aperçu toggle switches between the form and the letter, each at full width; - section tabs scroll sideways above the form; - a compact header holds the secondary actions in a "•••" menu; - Save stays reachable in a bar at the bottom. At 1280px and above the editor is unchanged.

userStories.title: Below 1280px, an Édition / Aperçu toggle shows the form or the letter at full width
userStories.description: As a user on a phone or tablet, I want to switch between writing my letter and reading it, each using the whole screen, so that neither the form nor the letter is squeezed.
acceptanceCriteria: Toggle. Below 1280px the editor shows a two-option toggle, "Édition" and "Aperçu" (localized in fr/en/de/it), under the header. It is a single-choice control with an accessible group name, keyboard operable, with visible focus and the selected option exposed; Each option is at least 44px tall; The editor opens on Édition.

Édition view. Only the section navigation and the form are shown, at full width. Every field of every section is fully inside the viewport at 320, 375, 768 and 1024, in en and de. This includes the Body section's add-paragraph button and hint, the rich-text toolbar and the sign-off select; No letter preview is rendered beside or below the form.

Aperçu view. Only the letter is shown, at full width, through the existing `CoverLetterPreview` (pane variant). It starts fitted to the width; Its zoom controls are fully inside the viewport at 320, 375, 768 and 1024; The whole letter can be scrolled into view.

State kept. Switching views keeps every unsaved edit, the unsaved-changes indicator and the selected section; The Aperçu view shows the unsaved edits; Switching back to Édition returns to the same section.
One scroller. In each view, there is no horizontal page scroll (the document's scroll width ≤ the viewport) at 320, 375, 768 and 1024.
1280 and above unchanged. No toggle is shown, and the three-column layout renders as before. Captures at 1280 and 1440 match the before captures.
FR-1: The mobile layout applies below Tailwind's `xl` (1280px), the resume editor's breakpoint. At 1280px and above, the editor renders exactly as it does after PR #120.

FR-2: One letter preview at a time, from the same in-memory editor state. The Aperçu view, the pane at 1280 and above, and the preview window all render through `CoverLetterPreview`; No second copy of the letter state is introduced.
FR-3: The menu's actions and the bottom bar's Save call the same handlers as the existing header buttons. No action logic is duplicated.
FR-4: The tab-strip behaviour exists once and is used by both editors (`CLAUDE.md` §10).
FR-5: Every interactive control: has a localized accessible name; works with the keyboard and shows visible focus; is at least 44×44 CSS px below 768px.
FR-6: No new user-facing string is hardcoded. Each new key exists, non-empty, in all four locales.
FR-7: No new dependency. Use existing Tailwind tokens, `src/lib/hooks/use-media-query.ts` if a hook is needed, and existing icons (lucide).

Regression constraint: At 1280px and above: the editor's header, translate row, three columns, Preview window and zoom are unchanged; `e2e/cover-letter-preview-window.spec.ts` (1280 tests) and `e2e/cover-letter-preview-zoom.spec.ts` stay green without edits to their 1280/1440 assertions.
Regression constraint: The resume editor is unchanged at every width. `e2e/resume-editor-responsive.spec.ts` stays green without edits to its assertions.
Regression constraint: Save, the unsaved indicator, Generate and Check (their modals), PDF and Word downloads, translation, and section switching behave as before at every width.
Regression constraint: `pnpm test:parity` and the exports are unchanged.

Regression constraint: Other specs that use the editor (`cover-letter-editor-i18n`, `cover-letter-pdf-export`, `cover-letter-docx-export`, `cover-letter-translate`, `sanitized-html-direct-load`, `cover-letter-template-language`) pass. Only locators that depend on changed markup may change, never their assertions; The preview-window spec's 1024/768 header assertions are rewritten for the new layout, as stated in Context.
Verification: The `CLAUDE.md` §14 baseline, plus `pnpm test:parity` unchanged.

Verification: A new Playwright spec for this editor at 320, 375, 768, 1024, 1280 and 1440, in en and de. It asserts: the toggle: its role and state, keyboard use, kept state and unsaved edits; field and toolbar bounding boxes in the Édition view; the letter at full width, zoom controls in view and the end of the letter reachable in the Aperçu view; the tab strip: `aria-current`, scroll-into-view and one-line labels; the header height; the menu: items, keyboard use, Escape and focus return, and each action's request; the bottom bar: visible while scrolling, never covering the last field, Save states; the notices in view; no horizontal page scroll; target sizes below 768; at 1280 and 1440, nothing new shown.

Verification: `ui-expert` rendered validation on the production build at 320, 375, 768, 1024, 1280 and 1440, in en and de. It includes: touch emulation; the menu open; both views, and a notice shown; before/after captures of both editors at 1280 and 1440, and of the resume editor at 320, 768 and 1024.
Verification: `code-reviewer` on each story's diff.

FAIL condition: At any width from 320 to 1279: any field, toolbar control, menu item, Save, a notice or part of the letter is off-screen, clipped, or reachable only by scrolling sideways; or the form and the letter preview are both rendered at once.
FAIL condition: Switching views loses an unsaved edit, resets the selected section, or saves.
FAIL condition: A menu action behaves differently from its desktop control: a different request, or a missing busy state or notice.
FAIL condition: The bottom bar covers the last field or the end of the letter.
FAIL condition: A capture at 1280 or 1440 of either editor differs from its before capture, or a resume editor capture differs at any width.
FAIL condition: The tab-strip logic or an action handler is duplicated.
FAIL condition: A measured target below 768 is under 44×44 CSS px.
FAIL condition: A control lacks a localized accessible name in one of fr/en/de/it.
BLOCKER condition: Extracting the shared tab strip cannot keep the resume editor's rendering identical. Report it with the differing capture; the owner decides.
BLOCKER condition: A Generate or Check modal, or the translation flow, cannot be started from the menu without changing its behaviour. Report it.
BLOCKER condition: The responsive spec cannot run because the local Supabase stack or the auth fixture is unavailable. Report it as a limitation; do not substitute another check.
Out of scope: Any change at 1280px and above.
Out of scope: The section forms' fields and behaviour, the formatting ribbon's own layout and touch sizes (shared with the resume editor), and the paragraph card's hover-only delete button.
Out of scope: The letter template, the PDF and Word exports, the preview window's own behaviour, and the zoom logic.
Out of scope: The dashboard shell, the sidebar and the "Dashboard-Menü" bar.
Out of scope: Other pages: the cards, `/cover-letters/new`, and the tools pages.
Out of scope: Swipe gestures between the two views.
Out of scope: Remembering the chosen view between visits.
Out of scope: A "Design" tab (there is one letter template).

userStories.title: Below 1280px, a compact header, a "•••" menu, and Save in a bottom bar
userStories.description: As a user on a phone, I want a one-line header and Save always within thumb reach, so that the form starts near the top of the screen and I never have to hunt for Save.
acceptanceCriteria: Header. Below 1280px the header is one row: Back is a 44×44 icon button with the accessible name from `common.back`; the title input is flexible and never overflows; then the save status, and a "•••" button with a localized accessible name; The header's height is at most 64px at 320 and 375, in en and de.

Menu. The "•••" button opens a menu with Generate, Check, Download PDF and Download Word, using their existing labels, icons and behaviour; It also holds a "Translate" group listing the four target languages, each with the same flag as today's translation buttons and today's accessible name; Each item is at least 44px tall; The menu has `aria-haspopup` and `aria-expanded`, and its items are keyboard reachable (Tab or arrow keys); Escape and a click outside close it, and focus returns to the "•••" button; Choosing an item closes the menu and does exactly what the desktop control does: same request, same busy state, same notice.
Translate row and Preview button. Below 1280px the separate translate row is not shown; The full-screen Preview button is not shown; the Aperçu view takes its place.

Bottom bar. Below 1280px a bar at the bottom of the editor area holds Save, full width or right-aligned, at least 44px tall; It has the same states as today's Save (disabled when nothing changed, busy while saving); It stays visible while the form or the letter scrolls; It never covers the last field or the end of the letter: they can be scrolled above it; It respects the device's bottom safe area.
Notices. The save-error, translation and download notices still appear, are announced as today, and are fully visible at 320 and 375; A translation started from the menu still opens the new letter.
1280 and above unchanged. The six header buttons and the translate row render as before. US-001's header assertions at 1280 still pass, and captures match.
